extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders and commenters on OSHA proposed rules (regulated employers, labor representatives, safety professionals, researchers)
extracted.subtask_short: filing comments on OSHA proposed rules
extracted.subtask_description: Locate OSHA proposed rules and the applicable comment-period procedures and content expectations (e.g., post-hearing evidence, topic-specific questions). Useful for preparing timely, substantive public comments on OSHA NPRMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 60-day comment period extension for listed NPRMs
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA is extending the period for submitting comments by 60 days to allow stakeholders interested in the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) on [various topics] additional time to review the NPRM and collect information and data necessary for comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 60-day extension language appears across many NPRMs in the listing. Affected topics shown on the page include: 13 Carcinogens (4‑Nitrobiphenyl, etc.), Acrylonitrile, 1,3‑Butadiene, Benzene, Methylenedianiline, Formaldehyde, Cadmium, Cotton Dust, Occupational Exposure to COVID‑19 in Healthcare Settings, Asbestos, 1,2‑dibromo‑3‑chloropropane, Methylene Chloride, Inorganic Arsenic, Coke Oven Emissions, Lead, Ethylene Oxide, Vinyl Chloride, and Construction Illumination. Practical implication: commenters should note the extended deadline when preparing submissions and may use the extra time to collect data, analyses, or other supporting materials intended for the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑hearing comment content and 30‑day extension (Heat Injury and Illness Prevention)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period to submit post‑hearing comments is extended by 30 days until October 30, 2025, to allow individuals and organizations who filed a timely Notice of Intention to Appear (NOITA) at the hearing additional time to file evidence and data relevant to the proceeding, including written responses to questions asked during hearing proceedings, as well as final written briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this specific proposed standard (Heat Injury and Illness Prevention in Outdoor and Indoor Work Settings), post‑hearing submissions explicitly may include: (a) evidence and data relevant to the hearing record; (b) written responses to questions asked during hearing proceedings; and (c) final written briefs. Commenters who participated in the hearing (NOITA filers) should prepare evidence/data and structured responses/briefs and use the extended deadline to ensure completeness and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Walking‑Working Surfaces: solicit comments on removing deadline and on ladder protection options
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule removes a deadline in OSHA's Walking‑Working Surfaces standard by which all fixed ladders that extend more than 24 feet above a lower level must be equipped with personal fall arrest systems or ladder safety systems. Additionally, OSHA is seeking comment on repealing or revising the requirement that employers use personal fall arrest systems on all fixed ladders over 24 feet tall and instead permitting employers to continue to use ladder cages or wells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should address the specific questions posed by the agency: whether the deadline should be removed, whether the requirement to use personal fall arrest systems on all fixed ladders over 24 feet should be repealed or revised, and whether ladder cages or wells should remain an allowable protection method. Relevant supporting material could include engineering analyses, incident data, cost/benefit information, and feasibility assessments comparing fall arrest/ladder safety systems versus cages/wells.
